task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 13, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about a new campus bus-pass agreement in Sable Crossing and what it changes for students and other riders.

facts.text: Sable Crossing Transit signed student-pass agreements with Nerith College and West Sable Technical Institute on Thursday, Aug. 13, 2026.
Beginning Sept. 14, enrolled students at either institution can activate a pass for unlimited travel on the system's local bus routes.
The agreements do not cover the separately operated regional express service or travel by faculty and other employees.
Nerith will pay the transit system $180,000 for the academic year and West Sable will pay $120,000.
Each institution will fund its contribution from its existing transport budget rather than adding a student fee for the 2026–27 academic year.
Combined enrollment is approximately 6,000, but activating a pass requires a student's separate request.
The agreement does not establish how many students will use a pass or how often they will ride.
A standard monthly adult pass costs $48; that fare will remain unchanged for other riders.
Students can activate a physical card at campus service desks without owning a smartphone.
Both campuses already sit on existing routes, and the agreement does not immediately add buses or extend operating hours.
The last weekday bus serving West Sable leaves campus at 9:10 p.m., before some workshops finish at 9:30 p.m.
West Sable has requested a later departure, but the transit board has not funded it.
Student council member Sora Penn works at a supermarket between morning and evening classes.
Penn said, "The pass removes a bill. It does not make the last bus wait for my class."
Transit director Daven Reed said ridership will be counted by boardings, with no academic records shared with the transit system.
Reed said, "We need to see which trips fill up before we decide where another bus belongs."
The institutions and transit system will review route-level boarding totals in January 2027.
The contracts run through Aug. 31, 2027, and renewal funding has not been approved.
The transit system operates 11 local routes and has used the same central transfer square since 2001.
Students already receiving a separate travel allowance should ask their campus office how the new pass affects that allowance; the two agreements do not set a uniform rule.
